headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images and call APIs, while the paired awesome-list has no runtime surfaces, so interaction risks are mostly indirect and limited by the non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible direct prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no io_surfaces, while agent_b processes documents/images and can run browsers, but there is no shared channel or default ingestion path between them in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_b output into a prompt for agent_a, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between the pair, attacker-controlled content could bridge them.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or clipboard automation between them.
Require manual review before reusing agent_b output.
Do not mount a shared MCP server or queue.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress, but agent_a has no data classes touched and no runtime surfaces. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or shared principal, so leakage is possible only through added integration, not by default.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, file contents could flow from agent_a to agent_b.
IF agent_b is configured to upload extracted document contents, sensitive document leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict agent_b to local-only processing where possible.
Review allowlisted egress destinations.
Avoid placing sensitive documents in shared paths.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. agent_a is non-runnable and exposes no filesystem or network write surface, while agent_b only shows allowlisted egress and browser use; without shared mutable resources, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory or shared OAuth scope is added, write conflicts could emerge.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable resource, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
Keep browser sessions isolated.
Separate any git or database credentials.
Use one-way handoff files only.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can consume documents and produce OCR/parsed outputs, but agent_a is an awesome-list with no runnable behavior or downstream action authority. There is no documented pipeline where B treats A's output as authoritative, so cascading error is limited unless an external orchestrator creates one.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent_a-generated text into agent_b without verification, errors can cascade.
IF agent_b's extracted text is auto-published or auto-acted on, downstream mistakes become more consequential.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before publication.
Require source-document checks for OCR outputs.
Do not auto-execute actions from parsed text.
Keep agent_a outputs advisory only.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for downstream consumers.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated data class is documented for either agent. agent_b handles documents/images and has allowlisted egress, while agent_a touches no data classes; compliance risk is therefore limited to future use with regulated documents, not a default violation.
conditions: IF regulated documents such as PHI or EU PII are processed through agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF agent_b sends document contents to a non-approved endpoint, residency or retention issues may arise.
mitigations: Classify documents before processing.
Block regulated data from agent_b until reviewed.
Restrict egress to approved endpoints only.
Document retention settings for outputs.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
